column1: # OCR-MODELS-2026-10-05: ocr-lab-round2, the candidates the 2026-10-05 survey found, fit-tested on this Mac (M3 Pro,
# 18 GB) the way OCR-MODELS-2026-10-04.tsv's header describes (same two pages, guard, fit rule, columns). Rows are
# added by each session of the item: `make-table.py $OCRLAB/results.tsv out.tsv <labels…>`.
# lab2-lighton (2026-10-05): LightOnOCR-2-1B ocr-soup and base have no MLX build, so they were converted here at 8-bit
# (ops/ocrlab/convert-mlx.py into $OCRLAB/mlx/, read as local/<name>) and their bf16 downloads deleted. All three
# read with no prompt at 1540 px and 4096 output tokens. Both conversions fit; the mlx-community 8-bit control
# was killed once by the guard on the crops (swap) and has its retry owed. At 1540 px every 8-bit LightOnOCR build
# peaks at 10.5 GB on the crops by MLX's own count, and swap growth decides whether it passes: the machine, not the
# model, is the margin. The guard's footprint peak reads exactly 11273 MB on every LightOnOCR crops run, 4-bit and
# 8-bit, killed or not; treat that column as suspect for these rows (it does not change fit: both are under 12 GB).
# lab2-churro (2026-10-05): Churro 3B read with its own system prompt, no user text, repetition penalty 1.05, and
# its XML answer reduced to text by ops/ocrlab/churro_xml.py (the Churro repo's extract_actual_text_from_xml,
# stripping tags where a cut-off read does not parse). The GGUF build was killed twice and is out; the MLX 8-bit
# conversion fits, at 1600 px (Churro's processor allows 4 MP). Its ordinary-page figures are the best in the lab
# so far, by rough-recall.py, which is a sanity figure and not the bake-off's score.
# lab2-infinity-falcon (2026-10-05): Infinity-Parser2-Flash read with its own layout prompt (its card: RL-tuned for it),
# its JSON answer reduced to the elements' text by ops/ocrlab/infinity_json.py. Ordinary page fits (5.1 GB); the crops
# were killed by swap growth at a 4.9 GB footprint with another lab job holding memory, and its retry is owed. Its
# ordinary recall/precision equal Falcon's to three places on different text (413 words against 409): the rough
# instrument's coarseness, not a copied file.
# lab2-olmocr-qwen3vl (2026-10-06): olmOCR 2 and Qwen3-VL-8B read with the plain default prompt; both fit, both
# looped on at least one newspaper crop. To make room under the 50 GB lab limit the LightOnOCR-2-1B-8bit control and
# Infinity-Parser2-Flash weights were deleted (both `no`, retries unrun); Qwen3-VL-4B-8bit (4.9 GB) still did not fit
# the limit beside the fitted builds and Archive Suite's weights in the same cache, and was not run.
